paragraphs: Applied Information makes traffic technology that turns intersections, school zones and connected vehicles into one real-time system. The customers are cities, which manage their traffic and ITS assets through a web-based application called Glance.

Glance monitors intersection cabinet equipment, reporting AC power, battery back up, cabinet flash, stop time, conflict monitor status, door switches, fan status and vehicle detectors. For emergency vehicles, an in-vehicle unit uses a cellular signal to tell the system a route has started. The system works out the route and talks wirelessly to the traffic cabinet to clear traffic ahead of the vehicle. School beacon flashers and their schedules can be viewed and controlled from anywhere. A connected vehicle product communicates over C-V2X, 4G LTE cellular and 900MHz.

The company states its hardware is designed, assembled and tested in Alpharetta, Georgia, with components meeting domestic content thresholds. A connected school bus system warns drivers approaching an active school safety zone or exceeding the speed limit. A smartphone app, Glance TravelSafely, extends the technology to residents.

quote.text: The drivers know they’ve got a green light in front of them, they know that everyone else has a red light, and they know the traffic is going to move ahead of them.
